description: We are Dream Space Travelers, a family team from Chicago! Dad Manikandan (software architect) and Mom Gracy help our kids Thanesh (10) and Mounaashree (8) build a game for the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. It teaches kids 7-12 how astronauts train: spacewalks, Moon base life, space weather, and flying to the Moon, using real NASA data. The kids designed it, tested it, and recorded all the voices!

details:
Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is a free browser game for kids ages 7-12 that teaches how astronauts train and prepare for Moon and Mars missions. Players complete 6 missions over 7 days — Spacewalk, Exercise in Space, Moon Base Keeper, Space Weather Watch, Moon Base Defender, and Earth to Moon Journey — balancing oxygen, food, power and radiation shielding, reading real space weather, and flying to the Moon, to become a Commander with a certificate.

The game uses real NASA data: today's Astronomy Picture of the Day and a real Mars rover photo fetched live from api.nasa.gov, and live solar-flare and storm reports from NASA's DONKI system powering Space Weather Watch, plus researched facts from RadLab, OSDR, Mars Trek and CSA toolkits (clearly labeled). If the live feed is down, backup real NASA facts appear — the game always works.

It was designed and tested by kids Thanesh (10) and Mounaashree (8) from Chicago, with help from their parents Manikandan and Gracy. The spoken instructions are Dad Mani's recorded welcome, with every mission intro read aloud by the browser voice. Built as a single self-contained HTML file (plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript — no framework, no server, no database, no account needed), with Web Audio sounds and music, browser speech, and progress saved on the device only. It works on phones, tablets and laptops in Chrome, Firefox and Safari (2016 and newer browsers), and plays fully offline.

Built with help from Muse (Remo), our AI assistant — AI tools used are disclosed here, as the challenge requires. No NASA branding or logos are used.
